articles.title: Courts Should Employ a Simpler Fair Use Analysis for Noncompeting Criticism
articles.description: Copyright and trademark rights act in tension with the First Amendment. Indeed, “unlike other property rights, [these] are a form of content-based, government-imposed speech restriction.” (Mark Lemley and Eugene Volokh, Freedom of Speech and Injunctions in Intellectual Property Cases, 48 Duke L.J. 147, 206 (1998)). As such, courts have determined that criticism, generally, puts the critic beyond the reach of a copyright or trademark claim.
